config.refreshIntervalSeconds.descriptio: How often to refresh usage data, in seconds.
config.currency.description: ISO currency code used to format cost estimates.
config.decimalPlaces.description: Decimal places shown for cost figures.
config.showLimits.description: Show your plan limits in the status bar: the weekly limit, plus the 5-hour limit if your plan has one.
config.useLiveApi.description: Fetch current plan limits live from Anthropic's usage endpoint (using Claude Code's own OAuth token — read from ~/.claude/.credentials.json, or the macOS login Keychain) so they stay accurate even when Claude Code hasn't refreshed its on-disk cache. Falls back to the cache file if the live request fails. Turn off to read only the cache file.
config.liveApiMinIntervalSeconds.descrip: Minimum seconds between live usage-endpoint requests. The status bar still refreshes on its normal interval; this only throttles network calls to the limits API.
config.showModelWeekly.description: Also show your most-used per-model weekly limit in the status bar (e.g. fable NN%), after your other plan limits. Requires Show Limits and a plan with a per-model limit.
config.showOpusWeekly.deprecationMessage: Replaced by Show Model Weekly, which follows whichever per-model limit your plan has. This setting still works.
config.showContext.description: Show the current session's context-window fill (like /context) in the status bar.
config.projectGroupingMode.description: How the dashboard's By project breakdown groups working directories.
config.projectGroupingMode.enumDescripti: Group by the enclosing git repository.
config.showCost.description: Show today's estimated cost in the status bar.
config.showTokens.description: Show today's token count in the status bar.
config.showExtraUsage.description: Show pay-as-you-go extra usage (spend beyond your plan limits) in the status bar and dashboard. Off by default; only appears when your account has extra usage enabled. Figures come from Anthropic's usage API.
config.predictiveAlerts.enabled.descript: Predictive alerts: project where your 5-hour limit lands by reset at your current pace, flag the weekly limit when you're on track to hit it before it resets, and warn before you run out. The 5-hour pace meter shows from early in the window (damped at first, firming up by the half-mark); the weekly ETA and the breach warning appear only once a window is half over and you're actively burning. A plan with no 5-hour limit gets the pace meter on its weekly limit instead. Turn off to disable all prediction features.
config.predictiveAlerts.windowMinutes.de: Trailing window, in minutes, for the tooltip's burn-rate readout (new tokens/min, cached context re-reads/min, cost/min) and for deciding whether you are still actively burning. The pace projection is derived from your plan-limit utilization and the wall clock, not from this.
config.predictiveAlerts.warnThresholds.d: Utilization percentages at which to show a warning notification for each plan limit, including per-model weekly limits. Each threshold fires once per window (re-armed when the window resets). At least one threshold is required; a window at 100% is always shown in the error colour regardless.
config.predictiveAlerts.predictBreach.de: Also warn when your current pace clearly projects you'll hit your 5-hour or weekly limit before it resets (e.g. "~20m to the 5-hour limit, before it resets in 1h10m"). Fires only once the window is half over, you're actively burning, and you're clear of the on-pace band — so it never contradicts a meter reading `· on pace`. Per-model weekly limits get threshold warnings only.
Show a 5-hour pace meter in the status bar: the projected end-of-window utilization at your current pace (e.g. `5h 23% → 45%`). A live 'how hard am I working' gauge that climbs toward 100% as you burn faster. It shows from early in the window — damped toward your current utilization at first so a thin early slice can't project an alarming number, firming up to the plain projection by the half-mark — and stays visible while you're idle. Reads `· on pace` within ten points of 100%, where the projection is too noisy to commit to a number. Turn off to hide it. (Set both this and Show Weekly Eta off to hide all forecasts.)
config.predictiveAlerts.showWeeklyEta.de: Show a forecast for the weekly limit. If your plan has a 5-hour limit, this is a time-to-limit ETA, shown only when your pace is clearly on track to hit the weekly limit before it resets, you're actively burning, and the week is at least half elapsed (the weekly number moves over days, so a constant readout would be noisy). If your plan has no 5-hour limit, the weekly limit gets the always-on pace meter instead (e.g. `wk 10% → 22%`). Turn off to hide the weekly forecast entirely.
config.predictiveAlerts.modelAdvisor.ena: Model-cost advisor (off by default): when recent turns show heavy spend on an expensive model for little output, show a one-time, dismissible hint suggesting a cheaper model for routine work. Requires Predictive Alerts to be enabled.
config.advisor.enabled.description: Show the Advisor panel in the dashboard: ranked, money-quantified tips to cut waste this month — routing routine turns to a cheaper model, improving prompt-cache reuse, reining in oversized context, and a month-end spend forecast. Computed entirely from your local usage data; nothing leaves your machine.
config.advisor.ai.model.description: Model used by the Advisor's 'Explain with AI' button (which calls Anthropic with your own API key). Sonnet 5 is a capable, low-cost default; use an Opus id such as claude-opus-5 for deeper analysis at higher cost.
config.advisor.ai.includePrompts.descrip: When using 'Explain with AI', also send a small, truncated sample of your recent Claude Code prompts so the advisor can coach on prompt quality. Only prompts from the folders open in this window are ever included, never those from your other projects. OFF by default — when off, only usage metadata (token/cost/cache numbers, no prompt text) is sent. You are asked to confirm each time prompts would be included.
